correctness.rationale: In the full single-edge subdivision H_n of K_n, original pairs have distance 2; original-to-subdivision distances are 1 or 3; two edge-vertices have distance 2 for intersecting edges and 4 otherwise. Hence a chosen subdivision-edge family is geodesically admissible exactly when its induced line graph is P3-free, i.e. disjoint cliques, corresponding to disjoint edge-stars and triangles of K_n. Mixed triples force no original vertex incident to any of >=2 chosen subdivision edges; singleton-edge exceptions allow one chosen endpoint but no other original vertices. The labelled exponential block formula gives exponent (1+z)t+t(e^{zt}-1)-zt²/2+z³t³/6, with n(n-1)z² endpoint exceptions, and maximal sets are partitions into singleton originals and triangle edge-sets. Independent all-subset BFS geodesic checks for n=3,4,5 (64,1024,32768 subsets respectively) reproduce each polynomial coefficient exactly; general proof is structural, not inferred from n<=5.
residual_risks: Finite computational checks corroborate but do not prove the unrestricted claim.

Earlier standard general-position polynomials and clique-component criteria cover definitions and structural ingredients but not this exact mixed-vertex enumerator for the incidence graph of K_n.
